messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the allocator RFC — I sketched a minimal runtime<->allocator interface for reuse/evict+compaction. want feedback on semantics and rollout.

maria: Problem summary: fragmentation from short-lived pinned tensors + heterogeneous alignments. We need an API that: (1) lets runtime mark ranges as reclaimable, (2) supports async eviction (background DMA to host or stream-offload), and (3) exposes a compaction hint so allocator can coalesce.

devin: high level +1. curious about sync vs async tradeoff: if runtime expects immediate reclaim we might block critical inference threads. what do you propose for backpressure?

maria: proposal: two ops: reclaimable_mark(handle, reason) -> token, and evict_async(token) -> evict_future. runtime can wait on future if it needs memory synchronously. default: don't block inference path; scheduler tries to free in background. explicit wait only for big allocs.

anjali: that seems reasonable. how does this interact with pinned pages and CUDA IPC? Eviction might require CUDA memcpy and invalidating GPU pointers.

maria: good point. plan is allocator to return a migration descriptor on evict_future completion: {host_addr, size, prefetch_hint}. runtime uses that for later copy-back. while evicted the original GPU pointer is opaque and invalid; runtime must use handle->map() which either returns live GPU ptr or a proxy that remaps after prefetch.

lee: can we see a tiny API sketch? inline pseudocode pls.

maria: sure — rough:

```c
// runtime -> allocator
Token reclaimable_mark(AllocHandle h, uint32_t flags);
EvictFuture evict_async(Token t, EvictOptions opts);
// EvictFuture can be polled or awaited
MigrationDesc evict_future_await(EvictFuture f);

// optional: allocator hints
void compaction_hint(AllocHandle h, int priority);
```

sam: flags: RECLAIMABLE_TEMP vs RECLAIMABLE_PERM? also need to indicate whether tensor can be regenerated cheaply (kv cache) vs heavy recompute.

maria: yes, add metadata tag fenotype: {recompute_cost: low/med/high, lifespan_hint_ms}. The scheduler uses it to prioritize evictions.

devin: what about fragmentation compaction? if allocator starts moving live allocations to defragment, we need to coordinate cross-stream sync and GPU kernel pointers. That's tricky.

anjali: allocator can expose a move_async(AllocHandle src, size_t dst_offset) that returns a sync fence. runtime must quiesce any kernels touching the handle. That's heavy but acceptable for scheduled maintenance windows or canary hosts.

lee: major worry: introducing these primitives increases coupling between runtime and allocator. Can we keep the interface small and purely advisory so alternate allocators (jemalloc-like on CPU or third-party GPU allocators) can implement stubs?

maria: design goal is minimal. reclaimable_mark + evict_async + a small set of tags + compaction_hint. If allocator doesn't support evict_async it can implement evict_async as blocking copy and return immediate MigrationDesc. That keeps compatibility.

sam: rollout plan? we need to avoid customer regressions; some models may rely on stable device pointers.

maria: rollout: v1 opt-in flag in runtime config --memory.eviction=advisory. Start with internal canary fleet, run perf and correctness tests. Then enable in dedicated customers as an opt-in. Also add strict mode for enterprise where pointers are never invalidated unless pinned explicitely.

devin: tests?

maria: unit tests for allocator stubs, integration test with KV cache workload that creates many small pinned tensors (we already have playback trace). Perf tests: tail latency, mem-overhead, total tokens/sec. Also add chaos test: simultaneous move_async + kernels to validate fences.

anjali: metrics we should surface: evict_ops/s, avg_reclaim_latency, bytes_migrated, fragmentation_ratio (free_extents / total_free), failed_evictions. Also track recompute hit rate when eviction used for KV cache.

runtime-bot: deploy-checklist generated: 1) feature flag + config, 2) allocator API shim, 3) unit/integration tests, 4) metrics + dashboards, 5) canary rollout plan

lee: one more tradeoff: evicting to host avoids OOM but increases host memory pressure and network egress on multi-node. we should add a global policy: prefer local host vs remote NVMe vs network offload.

maria: yes, EvictOptions will include target: HOST_RAM, LOCAL_NVME, REMOTE_STORE and a cost_hint.

sam: doc note: need clear semantics for pointer invalidation window — e.g., after evict_async returns a future, runtime must treat GPU pointer as invalid immediately, or is it only after future resolves? I prefer immediate invalidation so we don't risk stale access.

maria: agree. declare handle invalid on reclaimable_mark; handle->view() will fail with EVICTED until prefetch completes. we'll add a strict debug mode that traps illegal access in debug builds.

devin: ack. this looks actionable. my only ask is to add a simple diagram in the RFC: runtime path with fast path (no eviction), background evict worker, and on-demand wait path.

maria: will add diagram & lifecycle state machine. thanks all. I'll update the PR with the API and the initial tests, pinging reviewers when ready. :thumbsup:
